The transcript arrives ahead of the voice, so the next result was handed over while Moneo was still talking, and a user cutting in then cut off the wrong result. Moneo's voice is now metered every 100 ms: a result counts as said once Moneo has been quiet for 2.5 s, and the user talking before then means it was cut off. The audio-clock start of their words is compared with the end of Moneo's instead, and GPT-Live decides from its own transcript whether anything is left to say. I fixed the "still waiting for the second thing" bug and four smaller ones, and opened a PR to main: https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/134

**Your bug:** when Moneo started telling you the first result, it was also told the second request was still running and asked to mention it. The second one often finished while Moneo was still talking, so the "still waiting" line was out of date by the time Moneo said it. After that, the second result waited for 2.5 seconds of silence before Moneo got it, which was the pause you noticed. Now:
- A result no longer mentions other requests that are still running, so Moneo can't say something out of date.
- The next result comes after 1.2 seconds instead of 2.5, as long as the microphone stayed quiet. If you started talking, it still waits the full 2.5 seconds so it doesn't talk over you.

**Smaller bugs I found and fixed:**
1. **Corrections:** if you said "no, make it 15", Moneo still read out the old answer ("card for 12 euros") before the corrected one. Now the replaced request stays quiet.
2. **Greetings:** "Hey, how are you?" got stuck to the start of your next request, so the task list and chat showed "Hey, how are you? How much at Netto…". Now it's dropped.
3. **"Moneo is talking" label:** it stayed on after Moneo went quiet. It now follows Moneo's actual voice.
4. **Live call test script:** it was broken because it looked for the captions panel that was removed. It now reads what Moneo said directly.

The unit tests, lint and build all pass, and I added a test for each fix. I also ran a real call against GPT-Live. Moneo gave both results back to back with no out-of-date "still waiting". The test script's only failure was its own word-count threshold, which was too strict for a short answer, and I fixed that.

**Things I saw in the real call but didn't change**, so you know before showcasing:
- **Two requests merged:** for "when is my rent due" followed straight away by "I spent 12.40 at Netto", GPT-Live said "on that one too" but sent both to Moneo as one request. The answer still covered both, but it showed as one task in the list.
- **Wrong language:** when I typed a message in English with the mic silent, Moneo answered in German. With nothing spoken, it doesn't know your language yet.
- **Same words sent twice (not seen in the test):** if GPT-Live hands off a request without any new words from you, the app falls back to your last sentence, so the same question could run twice. I didn't change it, because I don't know how often GPT-Live does this.

Also, do take in mind when I was testing it, it might also be that I ask it for one thing.  It starts.  I ask for another thing that starts, and when it starts, saying for the 1st thing, I interrupted and ask it for a 3rd thing.  So that is sometimes how I test it as well.  So that thing is working as well.  If I ask it for the 3rd thing, it says, yeah, I'm checking into this as well and then continues from where it left off in the 1st thing, which is good.  The only thing is once it's done with the 1st time.  Then the things it says is like, okay, now I'm still waiting for the 2nd thing or something like this, which is not wrong.  Correct?


And the things you found  fix them as well

When Moneo went back to finish the first result, the app re-sent it with "still working on <the second one>" attached, and the second one often finished while Moneo was talking. content.text:
GPT-Live can't decide on its own where one request ends and the next begins. When it hands a request off, the hand-off has no text, and GPT-Live doesn't support tools that would let it write the request out. Since you didn't want an extra model, I fixed it with signals GPT-Live already gives, with no tuned waits:

- **GPT-Live replying marks the end of a request.** When it says "on that one too" without handing off, the app starts that request the moment GPT-Live replies, so your next sentence stays separate.
- **GPT-Live's own word timing decides the words.** Every hand-off says where in the audio the request ended, and every word has a start time. A word you started before that point belongs to the request, so "…this month" no longer loses "month".

I also changed how Moneo talks about requests that are still running:
- **It never says "still waiting" from an old snapshot.** Each result tells GPT-Live to say only that result. Once Moneo has finished saying it, the app checks what's actually still running at that moment and says it once. If the other request finished in the meantime, its result comes next instead.
- **It no longer invents an amount.** The quiet "finished, result is next" note I added earlier made GPT-Live announce "you spent forty two euros ten" before the real result, which said there were no Netto transactions. That note is gone.
- **Slow requests get their update again.** "Still working on it" never fired after the first result had been spoken. That was an existing bug and it's fixed.
- **Clean request text.** The stray "|" that GPT-Live puts in some transcripts no longer shows up in tasks or the chat.

In the last real GPT-Live call, every check passed: three spoken requests became three tasks, results came in order, nothing was made up or out of date, and the typed message was answered in English. The unit tests, lint and build pass. Everything is pushed to the PR: https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/134

Two small risks remain:
- If GPT-Live answers a half-finished sentence with a real reply (say "Sure, what do you want to know?" rather than a short "mm-hm"), the app would start the first half as its own request. GPT-Live is told to wait through pauses, and this didn't happen in testing.
- One test transcript had a garbage character in it ("cashഠ"). That comes from GPT-Live's transcription; I didn't filter it, because filtering odd characters could break other languages.
